Trever Nehls

Republican candidate for U.S. Representative, District 22, Harris County, Texas · Open seat

Chief of Staff to the interim Fort Bend County Judge; retired U.S. Army colonel; former Fort Bend County constable

Trever Nehls is a retired U.S. Army colonel and former Fort Bend County Precinct 4 constable who is running for the open TX-22 seat being vacated by his twin brother, U.S. Rep. Troy Nehls. He defeated Rebecca Clark in the March 3, 2026 Republican primary. In the November 3, 2026 general election he faces Democrat Marquette Greene-Scott and Demile James (American Independent Party).

Where Nehls stands

Immigration and border
Supports making President Trump's executive actions on immigration permanent law, finishing the border wall, ending catch-and-release, deporting people in the country illegally who break laws, and keeping cartels designated as foreign terrorist organizations.
Economy and cost of living
Says he will pursue policies to lower costs for groceries, gas, housing and other necessities. Supports lower taxes, fewer regulations and a pro-growth agenda.
Energy
Supports expanding domestic oil, gas and nuclear production and cutting regulations he says raise gas prices, in line with President Trump's energy agenda.
Education
Supports parental rights and full curriculum transparency. Says he would vote to eliminate DEI mandates, block gender ideology in schools, and restrict girls' sports to biological girls.
Public safety
Supports fully funding law enforcement and opposes policies he calls soft on crime.
Infrastructure and flooding
Supports flood-mitigation systems and studying ways to improve mobility in the Houston area. Lists finishing and expanding SH-99 through Brazoria, Fort Bend and Harris counties as a top priority.

Background

  • Chief of Staff to interim Fort Bend County Judge Daniel Wong, appointed April 2026
  • Fort Bend County Constable, Precinct 4, 2013–2020
  • Sugar Land Police Department officer and sergeant, starting 1993
  • U.S. Army, 33 years of service starting as an infantryman in 1988; retired as a colonel
  • Unsuccessful candidate for Fort Bend County Sheriff (2020) and Fort Bend County Judge (2022)
  • M.A., Military Strategic Studies, U.S. Army War College
  • M.A., Public Administration, Central Michigan University
  • B.A., Criminal Justice, University of Wisconsin

Also running for U.S. Representative, District 22

  • Marquette Greene-Scott Democratic
